title: What is the precise density of primes in short intervals?

problemStatement.formal: \text{What is the smallest } \theta \text{ such that } [x, x+x^\theta] \text{ always contains a prime?}
problemStatement.plain: Bertrand guarantees a prime in (n, 2n]. Baker-Harman-Pintz (2001) improved this to (x, x+x^0.525]. What is the optimal exponent? Cramér conjectures θ→0 (gaps O((log p)²)). Legendre conjectures θ just above 1/2 (prime in [n², (n+1)²]).
whyMatters: Central problem in analytic number theory
Connected to Riemann Hypothesis — under RH, θ = 1/2+ε works
Legendre's conjecture (1845) still open after 180 years
Cramér's conjecture (1936) would give optimal prime distribution

proven: Baker-Harman-Pintz (2001): prime in (x, x+x^0.525] for large x
π(2^m) ≥ m via iterated Bertrand (proved in Lean)
π(n) ≥ log₂(n) for n ≥ 2 (proved in Lean)
PrimeGapConjecture is monotone in θ (proved in Lean)
open: Cramér's conjecture: max prime gap O((log p)²) (open since 1936)
Whether PNT asymptotic π(x+h) - π(x) ~ h/ln(x) holds for h = x^(1/2+ε) unconditionally
knownResults.goal: Determine the infimum of θ such that PrimeGapConjecture(θ) holds.

currentState.focus: Formalization complete from PR #3130 — 0 sorries, surveyed open landscape
blockers: Cramér and Legendre conjectures are open problems with no near-term resolution

insights: Key Mathlib dependency: PrimeGapBounds.primeCounting_double_ge_succ for π(2n) ≥ π(n)+1
Iterating Bertrand k times gives π(2^k*n) ≥ π(n)+k — fundamental multiplicative density result
Since 2^(log₂ n) ≤ n (Nat.pow_log_le_self), the logarithmic bound π(n) ≥ log₂(n) follows directly
PrimeGapConjecture monotonicity uses Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_le for x ≥ 1
BHP (Baker-Harman-Pintz 2001) is axiomized — proof requires ~500 pages of sieve theory not in Mathlib
Cramér's conjecture and Legendre's conjecture are open — axiomized with correct types
PNT (π(x) ~ x/ln(x)) not in base Mathlib but in PrimeNumberTheoremAnd project
